''Dieffenbachia picta'' }} '''''Dieffenbachia seguine''''', widely known as '''dumbcane''',{{PLANTS|id=DISE7|taxon=Dieffenbachia seguine|accessdate=17 January 2016}} as well as '''leopard lily''' or '''tuftroot''',{{cite web |title=Plants & Flowers » Tuftroot |url=https://www.plantsrescue.com/tag/tuftroot/ |access-date=2 June 2021}} is a [[species]] of ''[[Dieffenbachia]]'', a [[Flowering plant|flowering]] aroid plant of the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Araceae]] (the arums). It is [[Native species|native]] to the [[neotropical realm]] of the [[Americas]], from extreme southern [[Mexico]] and [[Belize]] and much of [[Central America]], as well as the northern half of [[South America]] (it is typically absent in Argentina, Chile, Paraguay and Uruguay).{{Cite web |title=Observations • iNaturalist |url=https://www.inaturalist.org/observations?place_id=any&subview=map&taxon_id=206266 |access-date=9 April 2024 |website=[[iNaturalist]]}} It is found on many [[Caribbean]] islands and territories, including [[Cuba]], [[Grand Bahama]], [[Grenada]], [[Guadeloupe]], [[Hispaniola]], [[Îles des Saintes]], [[Jamaica]], [[Martinique]], [[Puerto Rico]], [[Saba (island)|Saba]], [[Saint Kitts]] and [[Trinidad and Tobago]]. ''D. seguine'' is also found on the [[Galápagos Islands|Galápagos]] islands of [[Santa Cruz Island (Galápagos)|Santa Cruz]] and [[San Cristóbal Island|San Cristóbal]], where it was likely introduced by humans. ==Description== Within the [[Araceae|aroid family]]—which contains other iconic genera such as ''[[Alocasia]]'', ''[[Monstera]]'' and ''[[Philodendron]]''—''Dieffenbachia seguine'' and its relatives, interestingly, do not grow as a [[vine]] or from a [[tuber]], instead growing vertically into a "[[bamboo]]"- or "[[Arundo donax|cane]]"-like shrub (hence the common name ''dumbcane''). Smaller or juvenile plants may only grow to {{convert|3|ft|m}} tall, while mature specimens can attain heights of up to {{convert|10|ft|m}}, and {{convert|2|ft|m}} to {{convert|3|ft|m}} in [[Trunk (botany)|trunk]] width.[http://www.mobot.org/gardeninghelp/plantfinder/Plant.asp?code=B589 Missouri Botanic Garden] . accessed 10.20.2011 The plant's leaves are large and green, often with variegated white patterns. Like the entire Araceae family, and indeed all ''Dieffenbachias'', the sap is toxic; the entire plant contains a high concentration of [[Calcium oxalate|calcium oxalate crystals]] which may produce negative side effects if ingested, potentially ranging from [[Anaphylaxis|anaphylactic shock]] and [[respiratory failure]] to even death. The plant produces the typical whitish [[inflorescence]] seen amongst aroids, visually-similar to those found on the common 'calla lily' (''[[Zantedeschia aethiopica]]'') or the 'peace lily' (''[[Spathiphyllum wallisii]]''), distinguished by a whitish bract ([[Bract|spathe]]) containing an inner [[Spadix (botany)|spadix]]. ==Cultivation== ''Dieffenbachia seguine'' is cultivated as an [[ornamental plant]] in temperate [[shade garden]]s and as a potted [[house plant]].
